hero.headline: A general-purpose backend for the cloud
hero.subtext: Para is an open-source, stateless and schemaless backend with a REST API over any database, search index and cache.

features.headline: Bring your own database. Batteries-included. No schema. No lock-in.
features.subtext: Para is built on several swappable layers. Start simple, then make it fit your requirements.

items.title: Schemaless objects
items.body: Plain JSON in, plain JSON out. No migrations, no ORM ceremony. Works on key-value stores and traditional databases alike.

items.title: Three layers
items.body: Every object is persisted, indexed and cached by default. Swap the database, the search engine and the cache independently.

items.title: Stateless scaling
items.body: No sticky sessions, no node-local state. Scaling out just requires more nodes, not a re-architecture.

items.title: Multitenancy
items.body: Each Para app is fully isolated and gets its own table, index and cache. Better efficiency and resource utilization.

items.title: Pluggable modules
items.body: SQL, MongoDB, Cassandra or DynamoDB. Lucene or Elasticsearch. Caffeine or Hazelcast. Choose per deployment, not per product.

items.title: Built-in auth
items.body: JWT, passwordless logins, LDAP, SAML and social login for all the major identity providers.

items.title: Webhooks
items.body: Signed webhook payloads on object events. Wire Para into anything that speaks HTTP.

items.title: MCP server
items.body: A built-in MCP server lets AI agents read and write your data directly, with the same permissions as any client.

items.title: Full-text search
items.body: Create complex queries using fuzzy matching or boolean logic. Results are ranked and paginated.

items.title: Geoloaction queries
items.body: Find objects by location, prefix or wildcard.

items.title: Automatic indexing
items.body: Every object is indexed automatically. Fine-tuning allows you to exclude objects from search results.

items.title: Resource permissions
items.body: Grant read and write access per object or per app. Para applies permissions on every request.

items.title: Validation constraints
items.body: Grant read and write access per object or per app. Para applies permissions on every request.

items.title: HTML Form handling
items.body: Add a contact form to your website quickly and securely. Para handles the rest.

items.title: File storage
items.body: Para supports file uploads using any blob storage provider. Choose between local, S3 or write your own.

items.title: Transactional emails
items.body: Use the special API endpoint for sending emails and notify your users when an event occurs in your application.

comparison.headline: Why not Supabase?
comparison.subtext: Para is a general-purpose backend, not a hosted database with extras. Different trade-offs, fewer lock-ins.
comparison.jab: Para was designed to provide a straightforward developer experience and is optimized for LLM-based workflows and rapid prototyping. Para is a good fit if you ask yourself any of the following questions:

questions.q: What if I don't want to manage a full PostgreSQL cluster?
questions.a: You don't have to. Para runs on an embedded H2 database by default, so a single JAR file is a complete backend with no external database to install or tune. If you need more, you can switch to PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB or another store through a plugin and one configuration property. On Para Cloud, all of this is managed for you.

questions.q: What if my schema is not clarified yet or my data is too dynamic?
questions.a: Para stores every record as a schemaless JSON object. There are no migrations, no fixed columns and no table definitions to update: you POST an object with any fields and the search index follows it. Add a field to one object and not to the next, or store different shapes under the same type, and Para accepts it without downtime.

questions.q: What if I want to connect a no-code solution to my backend?
questions.a: Para speaks plain HTTP and JSON. Any no-code tool that can send a REST request, such as Retool, Appsmith, n8n or Zapier, can create, read, update and delete objects with an API key or a JWT. Authentication, permissions and validation stay in Para, so the no-code layer only has to handle the screen.

questions.q: What if I need to prototype an app quickly with a set-it-and-forget-it backend?
questions.a: Start with java -jar para.jar and an embedded database. Users, social sign-in, permissions, full-text search and webhooks work on the first run, with no infrastructure to provision. When the prototype proves itself, the same API can move to a hosted or self-managed deployment without code changes.

sdks.headline: Use the client you know
sdks.subtext: All Para clients share the same REST API. Create, read, update, and delete a user, then search users with one query.
sdks.securityNote: Keep secret keys on trusted servers. Browser and mobile apps should leave the secret key blank, sign in, and use the permissions granted to that user.

features.title: Advanced authentication
features.description: Authenticate users with social accounts, LDAP or Active Directory. Para issues a JWT and applies resource permissions.

features.title: Full-text search
features.description: Every object is indexed automatically. Query by field, wildcard, geo point or more-like-this.

features.title: JSON API
features.description: Create, read, update and delete objects with a simple, secure JSON API. Pagination and field limiting are included.

features.title: Distributed cache
features.description: Objects are cached when they are created or updated. This speeds up reads and reduces load on the database.

features.title: Global scalability
features.description: Hosted on AWS inside a private cloud. Scale up and down quickly, with data replicated across regions.

features.title: Backup and restore
features.description: The paid plan includes backup and restore. Export a JSON archive and restore it when you need it.
